subject: PO metadata gating for volume discounts & weekly sweep pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@oakridge.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@oakridge.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO header requirements to qualify for volume tiers / weekly invoice sweep

Marissa —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement has a few non-negotiable gating items before Oakridge can accept discounted pricing or commit to a volume tier: they require specific PO metadata fields and prefer a weekly invoice sweep rather than monthly statements.

Key asks from procurement: 
- PO must include: Billing Entity (legal name + tax id), BU Code, Cost Center, and explicit Commitment ID (we use the field COMMIT_ID).
- PO header needs a flag: "WEEKLY_SWEEP: TRUE" so AP can automate consolidation.
- Net terms: Oakridge standard is Net60; procurement will consider Net45 if we provide an early-pay discount or pre-auth credit.
- They will only accept invoices with line-level SKU descriptions and a consolidated weekly PDF.

I attached our PO template and a short spreadsheet showing the weekly sweep flow (ap@oakridge.com asked me to include it). Can Redwood support these header fields and the weekly sweep pilot? If there are any system limitations (e.g., our PO token in your billing metadata), let me know so I can loop in our ERP team.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Lim
Senior Procurement Manager
Oakridge Systems

Attachments: Oakridge_PO_Template.pdf (PDF), weekly-sweep-proposal.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@oakridge.com>
Cc: Accounts Payable <ap@oakridge.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 May 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO header requirements to qualify for volume tiers / weekly invoice sweep

Sarah —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front: yes on line-level SKU descriptions and a weekly consolidated PDF; likely yes on custom PO header flags but need to confirm a few implementation details.

Internal notes for transparency:
- Our billing system supports storing arbitrary PO metadata tokens (we call them "po_tags"). We can map BU Code and COMMIT_ID directly to po_tags.
- "WEEKLY_SWEEP: TRUE" is doable from a tagging perspective, but the automation to emit a single consolidated weekly PDF needs a small billing pipeline change (1–2 sprints) to group invoices by WEEKLY_SWEEP tag and apply a PDF merge.
- Net terms: Finance prefers Net45 over Net60 for hosted accounts; for Net60 we would need to build in an early-pay discount or add a 1–2% financing fee. Vivek, can you confirm acceptable tradeoffs?

Proposed path:
1) We run a 6-week pilot where Oakridge sends POs with the WEEKLY_SWEEP tag. Redwood delivers consolidated weekly PDF and line-level invoices as requested.
2) Pricing: provide volume tier (5% at >$200k/mo) conditioned on POs containing COMMIT_ID and BU Code. For Net60 request, we offer a 1.0% fee unless Oakridge agrees to a 0.5% early-pay discount when they settle within 30 days.
3) Legal/Finance: we'll need a short amendment to the SOW that lists required PO fields and the weekly invoice process.

If that's acceptable I can draft the pilot SOW this afternoon and Vivek can confirm the finance treatment.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

Marissa / Vanessa —

Thanks for the context. Quick finance read:
- We can accept Net60 only under one of these two options: a) 0.5% early-pay discount for payments within 30 days, or b) a 1.0% monthly financing fee (one-time) applied to the invoice run for accounts electing Net60. Option a) is preferable for credit risk reasons.
- For the weekly sweep pilot, we will accept consolidated weekly PDFs but require the PO-level invoice subtotal to preserve tax and jurisdiction lines (our tax engine needs per-line jurisdictions). That means the merged PDF is presentation only; we must keep per-invoice metadata in the billing record.
- Volume tier eligibility: require 3 consecutive weekly sweeps showing committed volume before the tier auto-applies; finance will do a manual check for the first month.

Action items for Sales Ops / Legal:
- Marissa: draft a short pilot SOW and include a clause listing the required PO fields (Billing Entity, Tax ID, BU Code, Cost Center, COMMIT_ID, WEEKLY_SWEEP flag).
- Vanessa: can you get a quick sign-off from Legal on the SOW template? They may want to add language about changes to invoice cadence and early-pay discounts.

I'll be available for a call at 4pm PT if folks want to sync with Oakridge.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that path sounds reasonable and honest. Procurement is comfortable running the 6-week pilot. A couple clarifications before we start: 
- We'll add COMMIT_ID and BU Code to every PO; AP will set WEEKLY_SWEEP: TRUE for the pilot POs.
- Oakridge can accept a 0.5% early-pay discount if Redwood provides an invoice note that clearly shows the discounted net amount when paid within 30 days. Can your billing PDF include the discounted amount and the standard amount side-by-side for each week?
- For the volume tier: procurement prefers an automated check rather than manual sign-off after the first month. If you can auto-apply the tier after 3 consecutive weekly sweeps with the required fields, procurement will accept that flow.

Next steps for today:
- Marissa: draft the pilot SOW and a short amendment that lists the PO fields and discount language.
- I'll send over a sample PO populated with COMMIT_ID values.
- Vanessa / Vivek: please confirm if the finance team needs any additional evidence fields (e.g., AR aging snapshot) for the Net60 carveout.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Oakridge hopes to go live on June 2 for the pilot.

Best,
Sarah
